newsitem.title: SPAIN: Madrid airport reopens after fire.
newsitem.headline: Madrid airport reopens after fire.

text.p: Madrid's main Barajas airport reopened after a five-hour shutdown on Tuesday after the runway lighting system failed, an airport spokesman said.

The airport resumed normal activity at 2130 GMT, the spokesman told state radio. Authorities suspended all flights at 1630 GMT after a fire in underground electrical cables in one of the airport corridors cut off power supplies to runway lights used for night landings.

Barajas has been suffering severe delays in the last two months, prompting the airports authority AENA to enforce strict limits on the number of flights arriving and departing. The airport is Spain's busiest and handles around 20 million passengers a year.
